title: Clique colouring
description: Colour the nodes red and blue so that no maximal clique with two or more nodes has one colour only; existence is Sigma-2-complete (Marx). The check looks for a one-coloured maximal clique, and the refinement says that one of its nodes changes colour. With n = 5 the graph is a 5-cycle and there is no solution; try n = 10 (330 solutions).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The graph. Added to every solver.
fragments.text: % The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): colourings with two colours.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: every node is red or blue.
{ red(V) } :- node(V).
#show red/1.
#show blue(V) : node(V), not red(V).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: which nodes are red.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a maximal clique in one colour (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a clique with at least two nodes ...
{ q(V) } :- node(V).
:- q(U), q(V), U < V, not edge(U,V).
:- #count { V : q(V) } < 2.
% ... that is maximal: no further node is joined to all of its nodes ...
:- node(W), not q(W), edge(W,V) : q(V).
% ... and has one colour only.
:- q(U), q(V), red(U), not red(V).
#show q/1.

% Being a maximal clique does not depend on the colouring; having one colour depends
% on the colours of the clique's nodes only.
relevant(red(V)) :- q(V).

fragments.name: view
fragments.text:
% The graph; red nodes filled red, the others blue; a one-coloured maximal clique ringed.
#program scene.
draw(layout(circle)).
draw(node(V)) :- node(V).
draw(edge(U,V)) :- edge(U,V), U < V.

#program frame.
draw(attr(node(V), fill, red)) :- cand(red(V)).
draw(attr(node(V), fill, blue)) :- node(V), not cand(red(V)), kind(_).
draw(attr(edge(U,V), stroke, clique)) :- edge(U,V), U < V, cex(q(U)), cex(q(V)).
draw(emph(node(V))) :- lit(red(V), _).
draw(note("A maximal clique has one colour: recolour one of its ringed nodes.")) :- kind(reject).
#show draw/1.
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% The complement of a cycle on n nodes: two nodes are joined unless they are
% neighbours on the cycle 0, 1, ..., n-1, 0.
node(0..n-1).
edge(U,V) :- node(U), node(V), U != V, (U-V+n) \ n != 1, (V-U+n) \ n != 1.

% n = 5: the complement of the 5-cycle is a 5-cycle; its maximal cliques are its edges, so no solution.
node(0..n-1).
edge(U,V) :- node(U), node(V), U != V, (U-V+n) \ n != 1, (V-U+n) \ n != 1.

% The complement of the 10-cycle.
node(0..n-1).
edge(U,V) :- node(U), node(V), U != V, (U-V+n) \ n != 1, (V-U+n) \ n != 1.

% The Petersen graph: triangle-free, so every edge is a maximal clique and a solution is a
% proper 2-colouring; the graph has 5-cycles, so there is none.
node(0..9).
edge(I,(I+1)\5) :- I = 0..4.
edge(I,I+5) :- I = 0..4.
edge(5+I,5+(I+2)\5) :- I = 0..4.
edge(V,U) :- edge(U,V).          % the check reads edges in both directions

% A wheel with 7 spokes (hub 0, rim 1-7) and a pendant triangle 7-8-9.
node(0..9).
edge(0,I) :- I = 1..7.
edge(I,I+1) :- I = 1..6.  edge(1,7).
edge(7,8). edge(8,9). edge(7,9).
edge(V,U) :- edge(U,V).          % the check reads edges in both directions

generators.name: gnp
generators.description: A connected random graph G(n,p): each edge with probability p/1000; a disconnected draw is redrawn.
generators.text:
% gnp: a connected random graph with n nodes; each edge is present with probability p/1000
node(1..n).
edge(X,Y) :- node(X), node(Y), X < Y, @flip(p, X, Y) = 1.

reach(1).
reach(Y) :- reach(X), edge(X,Y).
reach(X) :- reach(Y), edge(X,Y).
:- node(X), not reach(X).            % a disconnected draw is rejected and redrawn
% the example's check reads edges in both directions
edge(Y,X) :- edge(X,Y).

#show node/1.  #show edge/2.

generators.name: gnm
generators.description: A random graph G(n,m): exactly m of the n(n-1)/2 possible edges, chosen uniformly.
generators.text:
% gnm: m edges chosen uniformly among the pairs of n nodes (pair I is the I-th pair X < Y)
node(1..n).
pair(X,Y,(X-1)*n - (X-1)*X/2 + Y - X) :- node(X), node(Y), X < Y.
edge(X,Y) :- pair(X,Y,I), @subset(m, n*(n-1)/2, I, edges) = 1.
% the example's check reads edges in both directions
edge(Y,X) :- edge(X,Y).

#show node/1.  #show edge/2.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 5):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction   options "--enum-mode=record"
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)
